lines.text: When you scan an item at the supermarket checkout, what is the red laser actually reading?
Most people think the scanner reads the black bars, but it is actually reading the white spaces.
A red laser sweeps across the code, and a light sensor measures reflected light intensity.
Black bars absorb laser light while white spaces reflect it back as a pattern of ones and zeros.
This binary sequence translates into a twelve-digit Universal Product Code number.
The register instantly looks up that code in the store database to pull up the product name and price.
That simple pattern of stripes automated the entire global retail economy.
